import numpy as np

def tensor(*args):
    '''Takes the tensor product of an arbitrary number of matrices/vectors.
    Input:
    args: any number of nd arrays of floats, corresponding to input matrices
    Output:
    M: the tensor product (kronecker product) of input matrices, 2d array of floats
    '''
    if len(args) == 0:
        raise ValueError("At least one array is required")
    
    if len(args) == 1:
        return args[0]
    
    result = args[0]
    for i in range(1, len(args)):
        result = np.kron(result, args[i])
    
    return result

# Test 1: Tensor product of two vectors
v1 = np.array([1, 2])
v2 = np.array([3, 4])
result = tensor(v1, v2)
print("Test 1 - Tensor of two vectors:")
print("v1:", v1)
print("v2:", v2)
print("Result shape:", result.shape)
print("Result:\n", result)

# Test 2: Tensor product of a vector and a matrix
v = np.array([1, 2])
M = np.array([[1, 0], [0, 1]])
result = tensor(v, M)
print("\nTest 2 - Tensor of vector and matrix:")
print("v:", v)
print("M:\n", M)
print("Result shape:", result.shape)
print("Result:\n", result)

# Test 3: Tensor product of two matrices
A = np.array([[1, 0], [0, 2]])
B = np.array([[3, 0], [0, 4]])
result = tensor(A, B)
print("\nTest 3 - Tensor of two matrices:")
print("A:\n", A)
print("B:\n", B)
print("Result shape:", result.shape)
print("Result:\n", result)

# Test 4: Tensor product of three vectors
v1 = np.array([1, 2])
v2 = np.array([3, 4])
v3 = np.array([5, 6])
result = tensor(v1, v2, v3)
print("\nTest 4 - Tensor of three vectors:")
print("Result shape:", result.shape)
print("Result:\n", result)
</parameter>
</function>
